evidence.detail: docs/spec/22.reverse-proxy.srs.md:1240 (SEC-PROXY-004 statement): "treat as `INVALID_RESPONSE` ... both `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding`, `Content-Length` elements that are not digits or differ, any `Transfer-Encoding` other than a single `chunked`" (no HEAD/204/304 exception), and :1252 (SEC-PROXY-004 AC-5): "A response with `Transfer-Encoding: gzip, chunked`, `Transfer-Encoding: identity`, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked;x=1` or an empty `Transfer-Encoding` value gives 502 with `kind()` `INVALID_RESPONSE`." vs :1179 (FR-PROXY-014 statement): "treat the response to a HEAD request, a 204 and a 304 as bodyless before any other framing rule, reading no body bytes in these three cases whatever their framing headers say" and :1192 (FR-PROXY-014 AC-6): "Whatever framing headers a response to a HEAD request, a 204 or a 304 carries, the proxy reads no body bytes and reports no `INVALID_RESPONSE` for those headers".

findings.description: Round 1 limited SEC-PROXY-004 AC-4 to responses that can carry a body, but the statement and AC-5 still apply to every response. A HEAD/304 response with `Transfer-Encoding: gzip, chunked` is INVALID_RESPONSE under SEC-PROXY-004 AC-5 and no INVALID_RESPONSE under FR-PROXY-014 AC-6. This also departs from the RFC 9112 §6.3 order fixed by PRD-150, PRD-155 and the request's §3.9 table.
